stem: A nursing unit implements a fall-prevention change as part of a performance-improvement project. The nurse compares fall data from before and after the change. What is the primary purpose of this comparison?

options.A: Determine whether the intervention was implemented exactly as written without considering client outcomes
options.B: Evaluate the impact of the performance-improvement measure on client care outcomes
options.C: Establish the underlying cause of every individual fall from aggregate unit data alone
options.D: Determine whether staffing levels should be changed solely on the basis of the fall rate

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places performance improvement within Management of Care and specifically includes evaluating the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use. Comparing outcome data before and after an intervention helps determine whether the improvement measure affected client care. A focuses only on implementation fidelity and ignores the stated outcome comparison. C overstates what aggregate data can establish about individual events. D makes a staffing decision from one outcome measure alone rather than evaluating the intervention's impact.
educational_objective: Use outcome data to evaluate whether a performance-improvement intervention has affected client care.

correction_summary: Removed the weak generic claim that public reporting of nurse-sensitive indicators is primarily intended to drive consumer choice and accountability. Rebuilt the item around the directly stated NCSBN entry-level nursing activity of evaluating the effect of a performance-improvement measure on client care, with an applied before/after fall-prevention scenario and parallel plausible distractors.
audit_findings: B directly tests the NCSBN performance-improvement activity. A is a process-fidelity question rather than an outcome-impact evaluation; C incorrectly claims aggregate data can determine the cause of every individual event; D makes an unsupported single-metric staffing decision. The stem supplies the intervention and comparison purpose clearly, B is the only best answer, and no second answer, cueing, unsupported threshold, or unresolved conflict remains.
